the design parameters of DC coil, AC coils, and the iron cores of the SI-SFCI are co-related, and the optimized design of the DC coil can reduce the size of the SI-SFLC by about 20%.
we have developed a method of optimizing the design parameters of a SI-SFCL to achieve the best performance and size for a given application.

the design of the DC coil and the iron core can be optimized for the 500 kVA SFCL, which will result in the device with the best performance in both fault current limiting and normal power transmission.

optimizing the design of the SI-SFCI, which is the most critical step in the development of the device.
the design and the performance analysis of the 500 KV SI-SFCL, which will be used for the demonstration project of a SFCL in the future.
the optimization of the design parameters for the DC coil, the AC coil, and iron core, and the optimization methods are presented in this paper.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a SI-SFCL with the optimized parameters of the DC and AC coils, and the iron cores, can be designed to meet the utility requirement of 500 kV, 20 kA fault current limiting, with a 10% voltage drop, and a size of 0.5m x 1m x 1.5m.
, for the 500 kVA SI-SFCL, the DC coil and the iron core should have the same size, which is the optimal design for the 500kV SI-SFCl.
the DC coil, the AC coil, and iron core can be designed in a way that the SI-SFCl has an excellent fault current limiting performance as well as a small size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the design parameters are optimized for the 500 kVA device, which are: (1) the DC coil's current density is 0.5 A/mm² and the DC coil's length is 0.6 m; (2) the AC coil's current density and the AC coil's length are 0.5 and 0.4 A/mm², respectively; (3) the core's cross section area and the core's length are 100 mm² and 200 mm

the DC and the AC coil should have the same inductance, the AC coil inductance should be as small as possible, the iron core should be saturated at the rated current, the DC coil should be as small and as thin as possible, the AC coil should be as large as possible, and the AC coil and the iron core should have the same length.

the design parameters of DC and AC coil and the iron core have a significant impact on the functional characteristic of SI-SFCL, and the optimization of these parameters can improve the device performances as well as reduce the size of the SI-SFLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SI-SFCl design should be optimized for the specific application, and the design should be done in a way that takes advantage of the characteristics of the superconductor, the iron core, and the AC coil.
a 500 kV 1000 A SI-SFCL with a size of 0.8 m x 1.2 m x 2 m can be designed to meet the utility's requirement.
